title: Indefinitely Working from Home: Use this Opportunity to Save Money.
summary: Learn practical ways to redirect savings from commuting and everyday expenses toward emergency funds, retirement and other financial goals.
body_text: Personal Finance Indefinitely Working from Home: Use this Opportunity to Save Money. 4 minutes read Posted: July 29, 2026 Remote and hybrid work arrangements have led many people to spend more time working from home, and some companies do not plan to return to office-based work. While you may view this as a mixed blessing, you can capitalize on the situation to save money for your short- and long-term goals. Your savings might not stem from tax breaks, but rather from other financial benefits. You won’t be spending money on commuting, restaurant lunches, after-work happy hours, etc. Now is a great time to update your budget and financial plans accordingly. You might be surprised at how much you’ll save. USA Today reports that remote workers can save about $4,000 a year by working from home.1 Other sources put the annual savings as high as $7,000.2 No offense to Starbucks, but just cutting out daily $6 lattes can make a big difference. You can also save money by not spending on a professional wardrobe, fancy lunches, and drinks after work. Think of the money you’ll save on gasoline (and/or public transportation). You can measurably improve your finances if you apply the $4,000 to $7,000 savings to high-priority items. Cutting back on child care costs can make a big difference. Although it might not be possible for you to work with children at home, with a little flexibility and creativity you may be able to cut down the time they need to spend in daycare. Consider taking the money that would have been spent on child care and funnel it into your Individual Retirement Account (IRA), or you could increase your 401k contributions to the maximum allowed, which is $24,500 in 2026, thereby ensuring you receive every cent of employer matching funds. Attack short-term needs first. Consider your immediate priorities. The first should be to establish an emergency fund with at least six months of expenses set aside. You may never use it, but you’ll thank yourself every day for the peace of mind it brings. Another consideration is insurance, both life and health. Setting up your life insurance plans involves a clear-eyed look at how much your family would need if you were no longer able to provide income. Also consider health savings plans and perhaps a better-quality health insurance policy. You can really improve your investment plans. Saving for retirement is important at any age, and the sooner you start, the more beneficial it becomes. Lest you think it selfish to sock away retirement contributions rather than spending the savings on your kids, remember that you don’t want them to have to support you in your later years. However, your kids will directly benefit by your contributions to a 529 education plan. Perhaps some family life events, like a bigger home, confirmations or bar mitzvahs, weddings, etc., will require long-term savings as well. Don’t fritter away a golden opportunity. Establishing a budget if you don’t already have one and tracking your spending closely will let you quantify how much you’re saving by working from home. Then it’s a question of clarifying and funding your priorities. Please contact our team to discuss your financial plans and how to help you make the most of your current situation. title: United Bank Promotes Zach Carlton to Triangle Market President
summary: RALEIGH, N.C. – United Bank recently promoted Zach Carlton to president of its Triangle Market. In this role, Carlton will lead strategic efforts to drive commercial and retail production and ensure the market's profitability and sustained growth.
body_text: Contact: Sameera Jordan Media Relations Manager Sameera.Jordan@BankWithUnited.com Facebook LinkedIn Email Twitter RALEIGH, N.C. – United Bank recently promoted Zach Carlton to president of its Triangle Market. In this role, Carlton will lead strategic efforts to drive commercial and retail production and ensure the market's profitability and sustained growth. Additionally, Carlton will play a pivotal leadership role in managing public relations in the Raleigh and Durham areas, while representing United Bank in the community through active participation in civic affairs and professional organizations. “Zach has consistently demonstrated the kind of leadership and commitment to his team, customers, and communities that we value at United,” said United Bank Regional President Jerry Ocheltree. “We are confident that the dedication and diligence that he brings to his work, as well as his willingness to take on new challenges, will continue to drive growth in the market and ensure United’s future success.” The Triangle Market includes three United Bank offices across Wake and Durham Counties. As market president, Carlton will continue to work from the Bank’s Raleigh office. Carlton brings 14 years of banking experience to his new role, including six years with United, where he most recently served as senior vice president and commercial lender before becoming market president. He joined United through CresCom as part of the Bank’s 2020 acquisition of its parent company, Carolina Financial Corporation. Prior to CresCom, he held various commercial banking roles at regional banks across the Triangle. “My goal as market president is to establish deeper ties in the region, while also building on the relationships that we’ve cultivated over the past few years,” said Carlton. “I want us to feel like a true community bank, staying involved in the organizations we are passionate about and getting in front of customers in the local community. Raleigh and Durham are both strong growth markets, so expanding our brand in the Triangle is an exciting opportunity for United.” Carlton earned a B.S. in business administration from High Point University and graduated from the North Carolina Bankers Association’s School of Banking. He was also notably one of 30 employees selected for United’s competitive four-year-long Leadership Development Program and was part of the inaugural class of the Bank’s Community Development Lending Program – an in-depth community development educational program for commercial lending employees. A Raleigh native and lifelong North Carolina resident, Carlton is very active in the local community. He currently serves as treasurer of the board for the Project Enlightenment Foundation, which supports early childhood development, and volunteers with the YMCA and Habitat for Humanity. He is also active with White Memorial Presbyterian Church, the Urban Land Institute, and the North Carolina Bankers Association. Zach lives in Raleigh with his wife, Barkley, and their two children. ABOUT UNITED BANK United Bank is a premier community bank and a subsidiary of United Bankshares, Inc. (NASDAQ: UBSI). United has consolidated assets of approximately $34 billion with over 240 offices located across North Carolina, South Carolina, Georgia, Virginia, West Virginia, Maryland, Ohio, and Pennsylvania, as well as Washington D.C. The Bank is dedicated to growing the relationships it has built since 1839 and offering a competitive suite of banking and lending products, treasury management, wealth management, mortgage services, personal and business credit cards, and more. Learn more about United Bank.

title: Hiring Temporary Staff for Diwali or Festive Season? Why Skipping Verification Is Your Most Expensive Shortcut
summary: Unverified seasonal hires increase fraud risks. Discover how to quickly verify temporary staff without slowing down hiring.
body_text: Insights & Resources Hiring Temporary Staff for Diwali or Festive Season? Why Skipping Verification Is Your Most Expensive Shortcut July 30, 2026 Shashank Yadav No comments yet Every year between September and January, Indian businesses go through the same hiring frenzy. Retailers bring on extra floor staff for the Diwali rush. Restaurants hire additional waiters and kitchen hands for the wedding and banquet season. E commerce platforms scramble to onboard hundreds of delivery executives to handle the spike in orders. Warehouses add packers, loaders, and sorters to keep up with festive demand. The numbers are staggering. Retailers and e commerce platforms see a 30 to 40 percent surge in hiring needs during the festive season. Forty three percent of employers report higher recruitment volumes during this period compared to the rest of the year. Warehouse helpers, delivery executives, store staff, and customer service professionals are the most in demand roles. And almost none of them are verified before they start work. The logic seems sound on the surface. These are temporary roles. They will be here for two or three months and then move on. We do not have time for background checks. We need them on the floor tomorrow. This logic has cost Indian businesses crores in theft, fraud, accidents, and legal liability. Temporary staff who are hired fast, given access fast, and never verified are the single highest risk category of employees. And yet they are the ones who receive the least scrutiny. This article is about why that needs to change and how to do it without slowing down your festive season hiring. Why Temporary Staff Are Higher Risk, Not Lower There is a widespread assumption that temporary employees are “lower risk” because their access is limited and their tenure is short. This assumption gets the risk calculation exactly backwards. Temporary employees know they are leaving soon. This fundamentally changes the incentive structure. A permanent employee who steals from the cash register risks their career, their reputation, and their long term income. A temporary employee who is planning to leave in six weeks anyway faces virtually none of those consequences, especially if their identity was never properly verified. Temporary employees are often hired in bulk with minimal individual attention. When you are onboarding 30 people in a single day for a warehouse operation, the temptation to skip verification is enormous. But that bulk onboarding is also the moment when someone with fake documents is most likely to slip through, because nobody has time to look closely. Temporary employees often receive the same access as permanent staff. A seasonal retail associate handles the same cash register, the same inventory, and the same customer interactions as someone who has been with the company for three years. A temporary delivery executive carries the same customer orders and collects the same cash on delivery payments. The access is identical. The accountability is not. Temporary employees are harder to trace after they leave. If a permanent employee commits theft, they are still showing up to work the next day. You know where to find them. A temporary employee who steals on their last week of the season simply does not come back. If you never verified their identity, you have no way to trace them. The name on their file might be someone else’s name. The address might be fake. The phone number might already be disconnected. The Festive Season Fraud Patterns You Need to Know Having worked with employers across retail, hospitality, logistics, and warehousing, certain fraud patterns repeat themselves every festive season with almost clockwork predictability. Cash skimming in retail During the Diwali rush, daily footfall and transaction volumes spike dramatically. More transactions mean more opportunities for cash to disappear between the customer’s hand and the register. Temporary cashiers and floor staff who know their tenure is short and whose identity was never verified are the primary risk. A cashier who skims Rs 500 per day across a 60 day festive season walks away with Rs 30,000 from a single store. Multiply that across multiple locations and multiple unverified hires, and the numbers become significant. Inventory walkouts Festive season means high value inventory. New product launches, premium gift sets, expensive electronics, and branded merchandise fill the stockroom. Temporary warehouse and store staff who handle this inventory have daily opportunities to pocket items. In the fashion retail segment, studies suggest that internal theft accounts for a significant portion of the 1.2 to 2.5 percent revenue shrinkage that Indian retailers experience annually. The festive season, with its higher inventory volumes and more temporary staff, sees a proportional increase. Delivery fraud E commerce companies onboard delivery executives at massive scale during the festive season. These executives carry customer packages and collect cash on delivery payments. An unverified delivery executive with a fake identity can mark packages as delivered without actually delivering them, collect COD payments and disappear, or steal high value items and claim the package was damaged or lost. The black market for delivery platform credentials is real. Unverified individuals purchase login credentials and employee IDs from departing delivery executives, allowing them to work under someone else’s identity. Kitchen and supply pilferage Restaurants, caterers, and cloud kitchens hire extra cooks, helpers, and servers for the wedding and event season. Temporary kitchen staff have access to raw materials, ingredients, and cooking supplies. Daily pilferage of a few kilograms of chicken, vegetables, or cooking oil might seem minor, but across a three month festive and wedding season, it adds up to tens of thousands of rupees. If the temporary cook is operating under a fake name and address, there is no accountability and no recourse. The Time Pressure Myth The number one objection to verifying temporary staff is time. “We need 50 people by Friday. We cannot wait for background checks.” This objection is based on the assumption that verification takes days or weeks. That was true when the only option was a BGV agency running manual checks. It is not true anymore. Digital identity verification through a platform like ID Verify by SalaryBox takes minutes per candidate, not days. You enter the candidate’s PAN number, Voter ID number, DL number, and UAN. The platform queries government databases and returns results while the candidate is still filling out joining paperwork. For bulk hiring, the process scales naturally. If you are onboarding 30 people in a day, your HR person or hiring manager can run verifications in parallel with the intake process. Candidate A is filling out paperwork while Candidate B’s verification results come back. By the end of the onboarding session, every new hire has been verified, and you have PDF reports for each one. The time cost is negligible. What is not negligible is the Rs 30,000 to Rs 3,00,000 in losses you prevent by ensuring that every person who walks through your door during the festive season is who they claim to be. What to Verify for Seasonal Hires (And What You Can Skip) You do not need to run comprehensive background checks on every seasonal hire. That would be impractical and unnecessary. But you do need to verify their identity. Here is a practical framework. For every seasonal hire, without exception Run a PAN check. This confirms the candidate’s legal identity against the Income Tax Department database. It is the single most important check because it establishes who the person really is. If someone is working in your store under a fake name, a PAN check catches it instantly. Run a Voter ID check. This provides an independent identity cross reference from the Election Commission. Comparing the name and date of birth across PAN and Voter ID gives you two source identity confirmation. For delivery, driver, and field roles Add a Driving Licence check. This confirms the licence is active, valid, and authorizes the right vehicle class. For festive season delivery surges, this check is non negotiable. A single accident involving an unverified driver with a suspended licence can result in criminal liability, customer lawsuits, and reputational damage that outlasts the festive season by years. For candidates claiming previous experience Add a UAN check. If a seasonal hire says they have done this work before, whether it is retail, warehousing, or delivery, the UAN will show whether previous employers actually contributed PF for them. This catches fabricated experience claims quickly and cheaply. What you can skip for seasonal hires Education verification, criminal record checks, address field visits, and credit history checks are typically unnecessary for temporary frontline roles. These deeper checks are best reserved for permanent hires, senior roles, and positions in regulated industries. For seasonal staff, identity verification across PAN, Voter ID, DL, and UAN provides proportionate protection at a practical cost. How to Build Verification into Your Seasonal Hiring Playbook The best time to integrate verification into your festive season hiring is before the season starts. Here is how to build it into your playbook so it runs smoothly when the hiring rush begins. First, make verification a documented requirement. Add it to your seasonal hiring SOP alongside other intake steps like collecting Aadhaar copies, issuing ID cards, and assigning uniforms. When it is written into the process, it is not optional. It is just another step. Second, set up your ID Verify account before the season starts. Create your account, familiarize yourself with the interface, and run a test check on a current employee to see how the process works. This way, when the bulk hiring begins, there is no learning curve. Third, integrate verification into the intake flow. When candidates arrive for onboarding, have them fill out a form that includes their PAN number, Voter ID number, DL number (if applicable), and UAN (if they claim previous experience). While they complete the rest of their joining paperwork, run the checks. Results arrive before the paperwork is done. Fourth, establish a clear policy for handling red flags. Decide in advance what you will do if a check comes back negative. If a PAN does not match, the candidate does not proceed. If a DL is suspended, they are not assigned to a driving role. If UAN contradicts claimed experience, a conversation happens before a decision is made. Having this policy in writing prevents ad hoc decisions under time pressure. Fifth, file every report. Download the PDF verification report for each seasonal hire and store it with their temporary employee file. Even though they are temporary, the documentation protects you for the duration of their engagement and afterward if any issues surface. The Cost Calculation That Makes This a No Brainer Let us do the math for a typical festive season hiring cycle. Suppose you hire 30 temporary staff for the Diwali season across retail, warehousing, or delivery. At under Rs 500 per candidate for a full identity verification (PAN, Voter ID, DL, UAN), your total verification cost is under Rs 15,000. Now consider the alternative. If even two of those 30 unverified hires turn out to be problematic, whether through theft, fraud, an accident, or simple incompetence masquerading as experience, the cost easily crosses Rs 1 lakh. A single delivery accident involving an unlicensed driver can cost Rs 5 lakh or more in legal fees, compensation, and insurance complications. Rs 15,000 in verification cost versus Rs 1 lakh to Rs 5 lakh in potential losses. The ROI is not 5x or 10x. It is effectively unlimited because you are preventing losses that could exceed your entire festive season profit. How ID Verify by SalaryBox Handles Seasonal Hiring Volume ID Verify was designed for exactly this kind of practical, high volume, time sensitive hiring. There is no minimum volume and no maximum volume. Whether you are verifying 5 seasonal hires or 500, the platform works the same way. You pay per check, so your costs scale linearly with your hiring volume. Every check runs against actual government databases. PAN goes to the Income Tax Department. Voter ID goes to the Election Commission. DL goes to the Transport Department. UAN goes to EPFO. No fake document can survive a database query. Results come back in minutes, not days. Your festive season timeline is not disrupted. Your onboarding session is not delayed. You verify and hire in the same sitting. Cross record analysis happens automatically. You do not need to manually compare four sets of results. The platform flags any inconsistencies between documents so you can focus on the ones that need attention. Every check generates a PDF report. By the end of your festive season onboarding, you have a complete verification file for every temporary hire. If any issue arises during their tenure, whether it is a theft, an accident, or a customer complaint, you have documented evidence that you verified their identity before giving them access. Do not let the festive rush become your most expensive season. Verify every seasonal hire at verify.salarybox.in Frequently Asked Questions Is it practical to verify 50 or 100 temporary hires in a single week? Yes. Digital verification takes minutes per candidate. With an efficient intake process, a single person can verify 15 to 20 candidates per hour by running checks while candidates complete other onboarding tasks. For 50 hires, you need roughly 3 to 4 hours of verification time spread across your onboarding sessions. What if seasonal candidates do not have all four documents? Run whichever checks are available. Most working age adults have a PAN card and Voter ID at minimum. For delivery roles, a DL is essential regardless. UAN is a bonus check for candidates claiming prior experience. Even two checks (PAN and Voter ID) provide meaningful identity verification. Should I verify temporary staff sourced through a staffing agency? Absolutely. Under the DPDP Act 2023, you as the employer remain the Data Fiduciary regardless of the sourcing channel. If a staffing agency sends you an unverified candidate who causes a data breach or theft, you bear the regulatory liability, not the agency. Always verify independently. What happens if I find a discrepancy in a seasonal hire’s documents after they have already started working? If the discrepancy is serious, such as a completely fake identity, you should suspend access immediately and consult with legal counsel about termination. If it is minor, such as a name spelling variation, address it through a conversation. This is exactly why it is better to verify before the person starts work. Prevention is always simpler than remediation. Can I reuse verification results if I rehire the same seasonal worker next year? Verification results are a snapshot of the candidate’s status at the time of the check. DL validity can change, UAN records will have additional entries, and PAN status can shift. It is best practice to run a fresh verification each season, especially for DL checks where licence status may have changed. Is the festive season too chaotic for a new process like this? That is exactly why you should set it up before the season begins. Create your ID Verify account, test the process, and write it into your seasonal hiring SOP during a calm period. When the rush begins, verification is just another step in an already established workflow, not a new burden added during the busiest week of the year. title: 19 Best One-Page Examples & Modern Website Ideas (2026)
summary: Explore 19 one-page examples and modern website ideas, from portfolios to product launches, with tips, tools, and FAQs to build faster and convert better.
body_text: Launching a new website can feel like a huge undertaking. Whether you’re a startup founder, a freelancer, or a creative agency, it always helps to look at successful examples for a little inspiration. Below, we explore 19 different types of websites, from focused one page examples to sprawling ecommerce stores, offering actionable tips and modern website ideas for each. Let’s dive in and find the perfect model for your next project. 1. One Page Website Example A one page website funnels all of your visitor’s attention toward a single goal, like a signup or a purchase, without any extra navigation to cause distraction. This simplicity is its greatest strength. Because everything a user needs is in one place, they are less likely to get lost. In fact, a study found that single page sites can improve ease of navigation, making visitors 60% more likely to return. These sites also tend to load faster, which is critical since 40% of users will abandon a website if it takes more than three seconds to load. Visitors form an opinion about your site within just 50 milliseconds, so a clean one pager with a clear message makes a powerful first impression. Many startups use one page examples for pre launch campaigns because they are quick to build and easy to adjust, making them one of the most effective modern website ideas Best for: Startup landing pages, event registrations, app announcements, and personal portfolios where a single, focused message is key. 2. Portfolio Website Example Think of your portfolio as a dynamic resume combined with a personal gallery. This is your chance to showcase your best work, share testimonials, and tell your story. A personal website is a massive opportunity to stand out, especially since 56% of hiring managers are more impressed by a candidate’s personal site than any other branding tool, yet only 7% of job seekers have one. A great portfolio builds instant credibility by letting your work speak for itself. It’s one of those modern website ideas that pays dividends for creative professionals. Recruiters might only spend a few seconds on a resume, but an interactive online portfolio can hold their attention for much longer. For anyone looking to build a beautiful portfolio without touching code, WeWeb’s templates offer the perfect starting point Best for: Designers, developers, writers, photographers, and any professional who needs to show, not just tell. 3. Creative Agency Website Example For a creative or digital agency, your website is your most important calling card. It must reflect your brand’s personality while showcasing a track record of success. It’s an investment that pays off, considering 75% of people admit to judging a company’s credibility based on its website design. Your site needs to build trust and generate leads. Exploring various modern website ideas can help an agency stand out. Trust comes from displaying expertise through detailed case studies and client testimonials. Leads come from strong calls to action like “Book a Consultation.” Many B2B buyers review around 11 pieces of content before even contacting a vendor, so your site’s content needs to be thorough and persuasive. Agencies can streamline delivery with WeWeb for Agencies . Best for: Marketing agencies, design studios, and public relations firms. 4. Marketing Agency Website Example A marketing agency website shouldn’t just be a digital brochure; it should be a lead generation machine. Structure your site to convert visitors by creating clear service pages for SEO, PPC, and content marketing. Each page should feature compelling case studies and prominent calls to action. This is one of the core principles behind effective modern website ideas for B2B companies. Your website is proof of your marketing skills. A modern, mobile responsive design is non negotiable, as 38% of people will stop engaging if the layout is unattractive. Since most prospects start their research on Google, strong SEO is a must. If your own agency site doesn’t rank well, it sends the wrong message to potential clients. Best for: Digital marketing firms, SEO consultants, and social media agencies. 5. Event Website Example An event website for a conference, webinar, or meetup has two main jobs: inform and convert. The essential elements are the date, time, location, schedule, speaker list, and a big “Register Now” button, ideally connected to a Calendly integration to simplify sign-ups. Using countdown timers to create a sense of urgency can also be incredibly effective, a popular feature in many modern website ideas. Since many people check event details on their phones, a mobile friendly experience is crucial. A staggering 76% of users will abandon a site that isn’t mobile optimized. Your goal is to make it as easy as possible for attendees to find information and sign up. Best for: Conferences, community meetups, webinars, and workshops. 6. Festival Website Example A festival website needs to do more than just provide information; it needs to create an immersive experience. Use rich media like highlight videos and photo galleries to get people excited. For a festival, an unattractive layout can be a deal breaker for 38% of visitors. The site should capture the festival’s unique vibe while being practical. Navigation must be crystal clear, especially for the lineup, schedule, and FAQ sections. These user-centric approaches are key to good modern website ideas. During the event, attendees will rely on your site for real time updates, so a fast, reliable mobile experience is key. Best for: Music festivals, film festivals, and cultural fairs. 7. Wedding Website Example Wedding websites have become the central hub for sharing important details with guests. The focus here is on personalization and convenience. These modern website ideas ensure guests have everything they need. Include a venue map via the Google Maps integration , schedules, dress code information, and registry links. An online RSVP form can also dramatically simplify headcount management. Make the site incredibly easy to use, even for family members who aren’t tech savvy. Use large, readable text and simple navigation. Remember that many guests will pull up the site on their phones for directions on the way to the venue, so a flawless mobile experience is a must. Best for: Weddings, engagement parties, and other large personal events. 8. Real Estate Website Example A real estate website needs to showcase listings beautifully and capture leads effectively. High quality photos and virtual tours are essential, as properties with professional images receive significantly more attention. An intuitive search function that allows users to filter by price, location, and features is also critical. Implementing such features is central to the best modern website ideas in this sector. One page examples are websites that present all their information on a single, scrolling page. Instead of using a navigation bar to jump between pages like “About” or “Contact,” users simply scroll down through different sections on the homepage. They are great for focused campaigns and clear storytelling. Are one page websites good for SEO? They can be. While it can be more challenging to rank for a wide variety of keywords with a single page, they can be highly optimized for a specific niche or keyword. Their fast load times and mobile friendly nature are also positive signals for search engines. When should you use a one page website? A one page website is ideal when you have a single, clear objective. They are perfect for event registrations, product launches, portfolios, or any scenario where you want to guide the user through a linear story without distractions. What should a one page website include? A great one page site should have a logical flow. This typically includes a compelling hero section, a clear explanation of the product or service, social proof like testimonials, and a strong call to action at the end (and often repeated throughout). Can I build complex one page examples without code? Yes. With WeWeb AI , you can build sophisticated one page websites with features like animations, forms, and database connections, all without writing code. How are single page examples different from landing pages? The terms are often used interchangeably, but there can be a subtle difference. A landing page is almost always a single page designed for a specific marketing campaign. A one page website can be the business’s entire online presence, just consolidated onto a single page.
